body.html: Lamlukka-Klong 2, in the Khu Khot area, is a residential pocket on the eastern edge of Pathum Thani where it meets Bangkok — a neighbourhood of working locals, with markets, local eateries and community temples. What Sena House Lamlukka Klong2 offers is a small place on Lamlukka 11 Alley that's genuinely quiet and set off the main road, which suits people here on errands, visiting family, or after a calm bed near Don Muang. For anyone who wants a quiet corner of this area rather than a room facing busy traffic, that's the main reason to pick it.

The property is a small studio building. Rooms are queen studios, available both as standard window rooms and as rooms with a city-view balcony. They're simply furnished but cover the essentials — AC, a flat-screen TV, fridge, kettle, work desk and an en-suite bathroom with a shower, hair dryer and basic toiletries. Real reviews most often praise the rooms for being clean, easy to find and quiet, good for actually resting — cleanliness scores on the booking platforms sit in the low 9s, which is high for a place at this price.
"Easy to find, clean room, nice and quiet, and the staff were very kind and attentive with daily housekeeping. Good value for a small place like this — the only catch is there's not much parking."

On service, Sena House plays to its strength as a small, personal place. A number of reviews call the staff kind and attentive, with daily housekeeping. There's free Wi-Fi, a lift, luggage storage, CCTV and security. But set expectations from the start: there's no swimming pool, no gym, no breakfast and parking is limited. It suits travelers who use the room just to sleep and head out to eat, not anyone after a full set of hotel facilities on-site.

The location is on Lamlukka 11 Alley in Khu Khot, Lamlukka district, down a quiet residential soi. It's about 11 km from Don Muang Airport, roughly a 20–25 minute drive, and within driving range of the Rangsit red-line station around 9 km away. Wat Pa Cittabhavana, the Klong Song community, a mosque and local markets are all close, while Future Park Rangsit and Si Mum Mueang market are a short drive. It works as a base for errands around Lamlukka-Khu Khot, or as a budget overnight before or after a Don Muang flight — but you'll want your own car or a ride-hailing app, since it's down a soi.

On scores, Sena House Lamlukka Klong2 does well for a small place, but to be straight with you, the review pool is still small. It averages around 8.9 out of 10 from real reviews — Trip.com puts it as high as 9.3 from just a handful of guests, with roughly 33 reviews across all platforms combined. The repeated praise is clean rooms, quiet, kind staff and good value. The complaints that come up are limited parking, a noisy bed frame in some rooms, not enough power outlets, and the odd report of a TV or bathroom issue — all the sort of thing you can run into at a small budget place.

Straight up, Sena House Lamlukka Klong2 sells cleanliness, quiet and value — not a long list of facilities. Its strength is a clean, quiet studio on a residential soi in Lamlukka-Klong 2 from a few hundred baht, close to Don Muang. If your trip is errands around Khu Khot, visiting family, traveling solo or as a couple on a budget, or an overnight before a Don Muang flight, and you have a car, it lands just right. But if you want a pool, breakfast, plenty of parking or a mall on your doorstep, look at the 3–4 star options around Rangsit instead.

A few tips from reading the reviews here: if you're self-driving, ask about parking when you book — it's limited and the most common complaint. The place is down a soi, so without your own car, plan to use a ride-hailing app. If you want a nicer feel, ask for a room with a balcony when you book. There's no breakfast, but local eateries and convenience stores around Khu Khot-Lamlukka are an easy walk or drive. And compare a few platforms before booking — it's a small property with limited rooms, so it fills up fast on long weekends.
